name: Cox's Bazar Beach
description: The world's longest natural sea beach stretching 120 kilometers. Cox's Bazar offers pristine sandy shores, stunning sunsets, and a variety of water activities.

name: Rangamati (Kaptai Lake)
description: The largest man-made lake in Bangladesh, surrounded by emerald-green hills and colorful tribal villages of the Chakma and Marma people.

name: Patenga Beach
description: A popular beach near Chittagong city where the Karnaphuli River meets the Bay of Bengal. Known for its scenic views and naval base.

name: Foy's Lake
description: A beautiful man-made lake in Chittagong surrounded by hills. Features an amusement park, water sports, and cable car rides.

name: Boga Lake
description: A natural lake situated at 1,246 feet above sea level in Bandarban. Surrounded by dense forest and offers a peaceful environment.

name: Chandranath Temple
description: An ancient Hindu temple located on top of Chandranath Hill in Sitakunda. It attracts thousands of pilgrims and offers stunning hilltop views.

name: Nilgiri Hills
description: The highest peak accessible by road in Bangladesh, offering breathtaking 360-degree views of clouds and mountains.

name: Inani Beach
description: A pristine coral beach near Cox's Bazar with unique coral stones and clear blue water. Less crowded and peaceful.

name: Ethnological Museum
description: Located in Chittagong, this museum showcases the cultural heritage of various indigenous communities in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

name: Himchari National Park
description: A scenic national park near Cox's Bazar featuring waterfalls, hills, and diverse wildlife.

name: Sangu River
description: A pristine river flowing through Bandarban, known for its crystal-clear water and scenic beauty.

name: Teknaf Beach
description: The southernmost beach in Bangladesh, near the Myanmar border. Known for its clean shores and beautiful sunsets.

name: Dulahazara Safari Park
description: Bangladesh's first safari park featuring Bengal tigers, elephants, and various bird species.

name: Moheshkhali Island
description: An island near Cox's Bazar known for its Buddhist temples and salt production.

name: Chittagong War Cemetery
description: A Commonwealth War Cemetery honoring soldiers who died in World War II.

name: Karnaphuli River
description: The largest river in Chittagong flowing into the Bay of Bengal.

name: Meghla Parjatan Complex
description: A recreation complex a few kilometres from Bandarban town, built around a forest-fringed lake in the hills. Known for its hanging bridges, cable car and boating.

name: Alikadam
description: A remote upazila in Bandarban known for untouched natural beauty and adventure trekking routes.

name: Parki Beach
description: A serene beach located between Patenga and Anwara, offering a quieter alternative to crowded beaches.

name: Jadipai Waterfall
description: A stunning three-tier waterfall near Keokradong in Ruma, Bandarban. Accessible via trekking.

name: Buddha Dhatu Jadi
description: The largest Buddhist temple in Bangladesh, featuring Southeast Asian architecture.

name: Nafakhum Waterfall
description: One of Bangladesh's largest waterfalls on the Remakri River.

name: Saint Martin's Island
description: Bangladesh's only coral island, known for pristine beaches and unique marine biodiversity.

name: Tajingdong (Bijoy)
description: The highest peak in Bangladesh at 1,280 meters. Offers challenging trekking routes.

name: Khyang Para
description: Traditional Marma tribal villages showcasing indigenous culture and lifestyle.

name: Chimbuk Hill
description: The third-highest peak in Bangladesh offering stunning valley views.

name: Hanging Bridge (Jhulonto Bridge)
description: Iconic hanging bridge in Rangamati offering scenic river valley views.

name: Shoilo Propat (Shoilo Waterfall)
description: A beautiful waterfall in Bandarban accessible via moderate trekking.

name: Batali Hill
description: The highest hill in Chattogram city, about 280 feet high, near the Tiger Pass crossing about a kilometre from the city centre. Its top looks out over the city.

name: Bayazid Bostami Shrine
description: A shrine complex dedicated to the Persian Sufi Bayazid Bostami, with a tomb in a brick enclosure, an old mosque and a large pond.

name: Anderkilla Shahi Jame Mosque
description: A mosque built on a high hill called Ander-Qila (the 'inner fort'), standing as a monument of the Mughal conquest of Chittagong.

name: Chandanpura Mosque
description: A city landmark known for its many brightly painted domes and minarets. Also called Masjid-e-Siraj ud-Daulah, it stands on Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah Road.

name: Chatteshwari Temple
description: A Hindu temple to the goddess Kali in the centre of Chattogram, considered one of the prominent Shakta pithas of Bengal. The city's name is said to derive from Chatteshwari.

name: Holy Rosary Cathedral
description: The seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Chittagong. The present cathedral was built in 1843, during British rule.

name: Zia Memorial Museum
description: The Old Circuit House, where President Ziaur Rahman was assassinated in 1981, now a museum.

name: Chattogram Court Building
description: A historic red-brick court house on Fairy Hill in the city centre.

name: Darul Adalat (Portuguese Building)
description: Better known as the Portuguese Building, this historic landmark was the city's first court building.

name: Bangladesh Railway Museum
description: Bangladesh Railway's only museum, in a former bungalow in Pahartali that opened as a museum in 2003.

name: Chittagong Zoo
description: A 10-acre zoo at the entrance to Foy's Lake, known for the first white tiger born in Bangladesh, in 2018.

name: Kattali Sea Beach
description: A quiet beach about 8 km from the city, known for its mangroves and the local fishing community. Also called Jele Para Sea Beach.

name: Banshbaria Sea Beach
description: A beach about 9 km from Sitakunda town, with a long walkway reaching out over the tidal flats towards the sea.

name: Sitakunda Botanical Garden and Eco Park
description: A botanical garden and eco-park in the forested hills of Sitakunda.

name: Baroiyadhala National Park
description: A national park beside the Dhaka–Chittagong Highway that keeps a corridor of forest for wildlife. Khoiyachora Waterfall lies inside it.

name: Khoiyachora Waterfall
description: One of the largest waterfalls in the Mirsharai hills: a chain of seven major cascades along a forest stream.

name: Mohamaya Lake
description: A reservoir among forested hills in Mirsharai, created by the Mahamaya irrigation project and completed in 2009.

name: Napittachora Waterfalls
description: A trail inside Baroiyadhala National Park known for its three or four main waterfalls.

name: Komoldoho Waterfall
description: One of the waterfalls of the Sitakunda–Mirsharai hills, a stepped fall over rock in the forest.

name: Hazarikhil Wildlife Sanctuary
description: A wildlife sanctuary in the Ramgarh–Sitakunda hill forests, about 45 km north of Chittagong port.

name: Sandwip Island
description: An island off the south-eastern coast, in the Meghna estuary. With Urir Char and Bhasan Char it makes up Sandwip upazila.

name: Banshkhali Sea Beach
description: A 37 km sandy beach, also known as Baharchhara Beach, with Kadamrasul and Khankhanabad as its main points.

name: Banshkhali Eco-Park
description: A natural eco-park of rolling hills, forest and a clear lake, looking out over the Bay of Bengal coastline.

name: Chunati Wildlife Sanctuary
description: A protected forest (IUCN Category IV) near the village of Chunati in southern Chattogram District.

name: Rangkut Banasram, Ramu
description: A historic Buddhist monastery in Ramu, known as the oldest Buddhist monastery in the country.

name: Sonadia Island
description: A small island of about 9 km², 15 km north-west of Cox's Bazar town, separated from Maheshkhali by a canal.

name: Kutubdia Lighthouse
description: An island lighthouse from British rule, built between 1822 and 1846 to guide ships in the Bay of Bengal. Storms have damaged it more than once, and it has since been rebuilt.

name: Shah Porir Dwip
description: An island at the mouth of the Naf River, on the maritime boundary between Bangladesh and Myanmar.

name: Teknaf Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Formerly the Teknaf Game Reserve, set up in 1983 as a sanctuary for wild Asian elephants. Its 11,615 hectares of forested hills include Naitong Hill.

name: Keokradong
description: A peak of about 986 m in Ruma, popular with trekkers, with a small shelter at the top.

name: Nilachal
description: A hilltop tourist complex run by the district administration at Tigerpara, about 6 km from Bandarban town.

name: Amiakhum Waterfall
description: A remote waterfall in the Nakshiyang area of Thanchi, one of many falls along the hilly Sangu River. 'Khum' means waterfall in the Marma language.

name: Rijuk Waterfall
description: A natural waterfall in Ruma upazila.

name: Ram Jadi
description: A hilltop Buddhist temple near Bandarban town, with golden spires in the style of Southeast Asian pagodas.

name: Prantik Lake
description: A man-made lake of about 2,500 acres at Holudia, formed by damming a local stream near the Bandarban–Chattogram border.

name: Sajek Valley
description: Called the 'Queen of Hills', a valley at about 550 m in the Kasalong range, known for its greenery and dense forests.

name: Rajban Vihara
description: The largest Buddhist monastery in Bangladesh, on the edge of Rangamati town, built by followers of the monk Bana Bhante after 1977.

name: Kaptai National Park
description: A national park of mixed evergreen forest, established in 1999 and covering about 5,465 hectares.

name: Polwel Park
description: A lakeside park in Rangamati town, on the shore of Kaptai Lake.

name: Alutila Cave
description: A 100-metre cave running through Alutila hill, surrounded by deep green forest.

name: Khagrachari Hill District Council Park
description: A horticulture park with a lake on the edge of Khagrachari town.

name: Shantipur Aranya Kutir
description: A Buddhist forest monastery in Panchhari, known for its large Buddha statue.

name: Shalban Vihara
description: Ruins of a 7th-century Buddhist monastery with 115 cells for monks in the Lalmai hills, in use until the 12th century.

name: Mainamati War Cemetery
description: A Commonwealth war cemetery for soldiers killed in the Burma campaign of the Second World War; one of two in Bangladesh, with the one in Chattogram.

name: Mainamati Museum
description: A site museum beside Shalban Vihara showing finds from the Mainamati excavations.

name: Kotila Mura
description: One of the most significant Buddhist sites at Mainamati, known for its well-preserved stupas.

name: Dharmasagar
description: A large man-made pond in Cumilla town, dug by the Tripura king Dharma Manikya I in 1458, with a Nazrul memorial beside it.

name: Jagannath Temple (Sateroratna Mandir)
description: The 'seventeen-jewel temple', one of the tallest temples in the country, built in 1761 and dedicated to Jagannath.

name: Shah Shuja Mosque
description: A historic mosque at Mughaltuli in Cumilla town. When it was built, and by whom, is disputed.

name: Kal Bhairab Temple
description: A Shiva temple in Medda famed for its 28-foot statue of Kal Bhairab, flanked by statues of Kali and Parvati.

name: Arifil Mosque
description: A late-17th-century mosque in Sarail, named after the saint Shah Arif.

name: Molhead, Chandpur
description: A riverside point at Chandpur's Boro Station where the Padma, Meghna and Dakatia rivers meet.

name: Hajiganj Bara Mosque
description: A historic mosque in the middle of Hajiganj Bazar, beside several madrasas and a library.

name: Nijhum Dwip
description: A small island of Hatiya upazila, its name meaning 'silent island', formed from islands that emerged in the estuary in the 1950s.

name: Bazra Shahi Mosque
description: An 18th-century mosque in Bazra, Sonaimuri, described as the most notable historical monument of the area.

name: Shah Amanat Shrine
description: The shrine of Shah Amanat (Amanatullah Khan, d. 1773), one of the most revered Sufi saints of Chittagong. Pilgrims gather in large numbers, especially on the 27th night of Ramadan.

name: Mathin's Well
description: A well in the Teknaf police station compound, tied to a 1930s love story between police officer Dhiraj Bhattacharya and a local woman, Ma Thin, told in his memoir "Jakhan Police Chhilam".

name: Debotakhum
description: A natural water-filled hollow in the hills of Rowangchhari, Bandarban, about 50 to 70 feet deep and roughly 600 feet long. Reached by a trek and a river crossing.

name: Gandhi Ashram
description: The ashram at Jayag, Noakhali, where Mahatma Gandhi arrived on 29 January 1947 on his peace mission after the 1946 Noakhali riots. It is now run by the Gandhi Ashram Trust.

name: Aggameda Khyang
description: A large Buddhist monastery (khyang) near the entrance of Cox's Bazar town, founded in the early 20th century by the monk U Pannya Jota Mahathero.

name: Debta Pukur
description: A small lake in Khagrachhari district, sacred to the Tipra community and also known as Matai Pukhiri, about 11 km south of Khagrachhari town.

name: Risang Waterfall
description: A hill waterfall about 100 feet high in Sapmara village, Matiranga, roughly 10 km from Khagrachhari town. Best in and just after the rains.
